findings.title: b-min-sep warm-start likelihood ratio misnormalizes the stationary mixture; the #748 confidence bound certifies the wrong functional and the add-direction PLD is anti-conservative
findings.claim: likelihood_ratio_warm computes `sum_f = f[0] + p*tail/denom` (denom = 1+(b-1)p), i.e. it divides only the barred-start terms by the warm-start normalizer while leaving f[0] undivided. The code's own remove-direction sampler `sample_x_under_p` (mc.rs:85-108) draws the initial barred state from the stationary distribution P(state 0)=1/denom, P(state j)=p/denom, whose exact density ratio is (f[0] + p*sum_{j=1}^{b-1} f[j])/denom. The coded expression is therefore not the likelihood ratio of ANY initial-state mixture (its E_Q would need weights summing to 1+(b-1)p/denom > 1). Consequently the Monte Carlo 'privacy loss' samples fed into the PR #748 confidence-band machinery (samples_to_pmf) are ln of an inflated statistic, not the true log-likelihood ratio: the remove-direction PLD is inflated (still an upper bound, but systematically loose by up to ~ln(1+(b-1)p)), and the add-direction PLD is shifted DOWN, so the add-direction epsilon/delta certificate is invalid (underestimates the true add-direction hockey-stick). The final epsilon = max(remove, add); when the deflated add side binds (possible after composing the asymmetric MC PLD with other mechanisms, or in configs where add dominates), the reported 'high-confidence bound' understates the true epsilon. This is reachable from the public API via opaque.dpftrl.accounting.b_min_sep (packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpftrl/amplification/_b_min_sep/__init__.py:191-214 calls _native.bandmf_b_min_sep_warm_mc_pld / bandmf_b_min_sep_pld_from_transcript_handle), and the July audit's closed issue #337 ('Return conservative privacy guarantees from Monte Carlo amplification', claimed fixed by #748) is therefore incompletely fixed on this path. The runtime BMinSepSampler also uses the stationary warm start (July audit master list line 158 verified P(eligible)=1/(1+(b-1)p)), so the accountant's functional mismatches the deployed mechanism, not just its own internal sampler. The bug predates the audit (introduced in commit 5de05eb0, PR #121) and survived both the audit and PR #748, which rewrote the surrounding sample-to-PMF pipeline without touching these four lines. Distinct from open issue #697 (prefix tightness / MC-error certification): this is a wrong likelihood-ratio functional, not an uncertified error.
findings.failure_scenario: User configures BandMF with b-min-sep sampling, e.g. bands=2, p=0.05, n=50, sigma=1.0 (the repo's own mc_pld_smoke configuration). Faithful Python reimplementation of the Rust code (verified line-by-line against mc.rs:25-76): E_Q[r_code] = 1.16647 +/- 0.003 vs required 1.0 (analytic prediction 1+(b-1)p/denom = 1.16667 at p=0.2); importance-sampling identity P[ln r > t] = E_Q[r*1{ln r>t}] fails for the coded r (0.4597 vs 0.5366 at t=0.5) and holds for the corrected r (0.3939 vs 0.3939). Epsilon impact at delta=0.01 (plain-MC hockey stick, 60k samples): CODE eps_remove=1.286 / eps_add=0.720 vs TRUE eps_remove=1.239 / eps_add=0.766 -- the standalone reported max is inflated ~4% (silent over-noising after calibration), and the add-direction certificate underestimates the true add epsilon by ~6%; with larger bands*p (e.g. bands=32, p=0.02, denom=1.62) the remove inflation grows toward ln(1.62)~0.48 whole-run epsilon while the add deficit grows symmetrically. In any composition where the add adjacency binds the composed maximum, the returned '1-mc_failure_probability confidence' epsilon is below the true epsilon: silent privacy loss.
evidence: packages/opaque-accounting/src/amplification/b_min_sep/mc.rs:69-75: `let denom = 1.0 + (bands.saturating_sub(1) as f64) * p; let mut sum_f = f[0]; if bands > 1 { let tail: f64 = (1..bands).map(|j| f[j]).sum::<f64>(); sum_f += p * tail / denom; } sum_f` -- f[0] is not divided by denom.

packages/opaque-accounting/src/amplification/b_min_sep/mc.rs:87-96 (sample_x_under_p): `let denom = 1.0 + (bands - 1) as f64 * p; if rng.random::<f64>() * denom < 1.0 { 0 } else { 1 + rng.random_range(0..bands - 1) }` -- initial state 0 has probability 1/denom, states 1..b-1 have p/denom each; the mixture ratio consistent with this sampler is (f[0]+p*sum f[j])/denom.

Numerical check (scratchpad/check_lr_warm.py, faithful reimplementation, numpy 2.1.3): E_Q[r_code]=1.16647 (se 0.003) vs analytic 1+(b-1)p/denom=1.16667; E_Q[r_true]=0.99982. IS-consistency holds only for the corrected formula (t=0.5: TRUE 0.3939 vs 0.3939; CODE 0.4597 vs 0.5366).

Epsilon quantification (scratchpad/check_lr_eps.py): delta=0.01 -> CODE eps_remove=1.2858/eps_add=0.7195, TRUE eps_remove=1.2393/eps_add=0.7660; add-direction delta at eps=0.3: code 0.14870 vs true 0.19815 (25% underestimate).

mc.rs:389,409-410: remove samples `r.ln()` with y ~ P via sample_x_under_p, add samples `-(r.ln())` with y ~ Q -- both use the same wrong r, so the constructed asymmetric PLD is the confidence band of the wrong statistic in both directions.

findings.fix_sketch: In likelihood_ratio_warm, divide the full mixture by denom: `sum_f = (f[0] + p * tail) / denom` (with tail=0 when bands==1). Add a normalization test asserting the empirical E_Q[likelihood_ratio_warm] ~= 1 over Q-samples for bands in {2,4,8}, and an oracle test for bands=1 asserting the MC bound dominates poisson_gaussian_pld(sigma,p).self_compose(n). Re-derive expected epsilon shifts and add a regression vector (fits open issue #666's remit).

findings.title: b-min-sep Monte Carlo epsilon depends on Rayon thread count with a fixed seed -- the #331 reproducibility fix covered only balls-in-bins, not the sibling sampler PR #748 also touched
findings.claim: Closed issue #331 ('Make balls-in-bins Monte Carlo reproducible across thread counts') was fixed by giving bnb_mc_pld fixed 1024-sample shards whose seeds depend only on the shard index (monte_carlo.rs:43-55: 'The shard count must depend only on the resolved sample count, not on the Rayon worker count: users expect a fixed seed to select the same samples on every machine'). The sibling MC sampler bandmf_b_min_sep_warm_mc_pld -- rewritten by the same PR #748 for the confidence-bound plumbing -- still partitions its RNG streams by `rayon::current_num_threads()` and seeds per-thread StdRngs as seed+tid (remove) and seed+1000+tid (add), so the drawn sample set, and therefore the reported epsilon, changes with the machine's core count. bandmf_b_min_sep_prepare_transcripts (mc.rs:174-218) has the same dependence even though it runs serially (it deliberately mirrors the thread partition), so cached transcript corpora prepared on one machine differ from another; the Python transcript cache key (packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpftrl/amplification/_b_min_sep/_transcript_cache.py:32 `key = (strategy_coef, n_steps, p, num_mc_samples, mc_seed)`) does not capture the thread count, so identical keys map to different corpora across environments. Reproducibility is a documented contract of `seed` ('RNG seed for Monte Carlo reproducibility', discretization.py:25/123) and the only regression test (tests/test_balls_in_bins_reproducible.py) covers balls-in-bins alone. Additionally, seed+1000+tid collides with the remove streams whenever current_num_threads() > 1000 (remove tid=1000 equals add tid=0), which would reuse identical randomness across adjacency directions on very large machines.
findings.failure_scenario: Measured on this tree (RAYON_NUM_THREADS in {1,2,8}, seed=173, coef=[sqrt(0.7),sqrt(0.3)], n=50, p=0.05, sigma=1.0, mc_resolution=5e-3, mc_failure_probability=1e-2): epsilon_at(1e-2) = 1.5789 (1 thread), 1.5938 (2 threads), 1.8443 (8 threads) -- a 17% swing in the reported guarantee from the core count alone. A team pinning seed=42 in CI on a 4-core runner and deploying calibration on a 64-core box gets a different noise multiplier for the 'same' configuration; privacy statements citing a specific (epsilon, delta, seed) triple are not verifiable on other hardware. Each individual value is still a valid confidence bound for its own sample set (given finding 1 is fixed), so this is silent nondeterminism of the reported guarantee rather than an invalid bound.
evidence: packages/opaque-accounting/src/amplification/b_min_sep/mc.rs:364-366: `let n_threads = rayon::current_num_threads().max(1); let samples_per_thread = num_samples / n_threads; let remainder = num_samples - samples_per_thread * n_threads;`

mc.rs:378: `let mut rng = StdRng::seed_from_u64(seed.wrapping_add(tid as u64));` (remove) and mc.rs:404: `seed.wrapping_add(1000 + tid as u64)` (add) -- streams indexed by tid, whose count is the live Rayon pool size.

mc.rs:174: prepare_transcripts: `let n_threads = rayon::current_num_threads().max(1);` with the same per-tid seeding at :187 and :210; doc comment :147 explicitly states 'Sample order matches ... with the same per-thread StdRng seeds (seed+tid and 1000+tid)'.

Contrast the fixed sibling: balls_in_bins/monte_carlo.rs:43-55 SAMPLES_PER_SHARD=1024 with shard_seed(seed, shard, add_direction)=seed+shard*2+dir, plus test_bnb_mc_pld_is_identical_across_thread_counts (monte_carlo.rs:549-596) and tests/test_balls_in_bins_reproducible.py -- no analogous mechanism or test for b_min_sep.

issues-closed-audit.tsv:331 'Make balls-in-bins Monte Carlo reproducible across thread counts' (closed); open issues #666/#697 do not cover reproducibility.
findings.fix_sketch: Port the balls-in-bins shard scheme: draw remove/add samples in fixed-size shards (par_chunks_mut(SAMPLES_PER_SHARD)) seeded by shard index and direction only, for both bandmf_b_min_sep_warm_mc_pld and bandmf_b_min_sep_prepare_transcripts (keeping the prefix-projection property: seed each per-sample row or shard independently of the pool size). Extend tests/test_balls_in_bins_reproducible.py to cover bandmf_b_min_sep_warm_mc_pld across RAYON_NUM_THREADS. Use a domain-separated direction offset (e.g. odd/even like shard_seed) instead of +1000 to remove the >1000-thread collision.

clean_areas: Checked the concentration inequality powering the confidence band by re-deriving it: for any F (atoms included), P[F(X_(rank)) < p] <= P[Bin(n,p) >= rank] <= exp(-n*KL(rank/n||p)) (Chernoff-Hoeffding); kl_lower_cdf_bound (monte_carlo.rs:395-420) bisects the monotone-decreasing KL on [0, rank/n] and keeps the lower (conservative) side; binary_kl handles q>=1 as -ln p correctly; test_kl_band_is_below_exact_order_statistic_bound cross-checks against exact Beta(rank, n-rank+1) inversion and passes on this tree.

Checked the band is applied to the right functional and one-sided in the safe direction for balls-in-bins by re-deriving Choquette-Choo et al. (2024) Lemma 3.2 after Gram reduction: remove-direction Y = log((1/b) sum_k exp((2u_k - G_kk)/(2 sigma^2))) with u ~ N(G_i., sigma^2 G) and add-direction -Y with u ~ N(0, sigma^2 G) match monte_carlo.rs:61-134 exactly; samples_to_pmf shifts mass only upward (ceil bucketing to loss = index*discretization per Pmf convention confirmed in realization.rs:114-118 and pmf/mod.rs:103-123; lower confidence CDF -> constructed variable stochastically dominates the true loss), which upper-bounds every hockey-stick metric since (1 - a*e^{-L})_+ is nondecreasing in L; residual mass goes to +infinity (safe).

Checked resolved_num_mc_samples (discretization/config.rs:150-183) algebra: final-rank residual 1-(failure/(2n))^{1/n} equals `-(per_rank.ln()/n).exp_m1()`; binary search returns the minimal n; samples_to_pmf fails closed when achieved infinity_mass exceeds requested mc_resolution (monte_carlo.rs:374-381) and when total mass deviates from 1 by >1e-9; non-finite samples now hard-error instead of silently vanishing (monte_carlo.rs:282-295, regression of the pre-audit mass-loss bug).

Checked union-bound bookkeeping: per-rank failure = failure/(num_directions*n) with num_directions=2 passed by both bnb_mc_pld and the b_min_sep entry points, covering all n ranks in each of the two adjacency directions; monotone CDF enforcement via cdf_bound.max(previous) at monte_carlo.rs:366.

Ran numerical oracle checks: (a) identity-Gram BnB MC bound >= exact random_allocation_gaussian_pld at deltas 6e-3..5e-2 (e.g. 1.477 vs 1.109 at delta=1e-2); (b) bands=1 b-min-sep MC bound >= analytic poisson_gaussian_pld(sigma,p).self_compose(n) at three deltas; (c) epsilon_at(delta <= infinity_mass) returns inf and epsilon_at just above it is finite; the shipped Rust test suite for monte_carlo (13 tests) and b_min_sep (4 tests) passes on this tree.

Checked fail-closed behavior of non-certified metrics: beta_at returns 0.0 and risk_at returns 0.0 for any PLD with estimation_failure_probability > 0 (pld/mod.rs:355-359, 403-406) -- the attacker-perfect, privacy-safe direction; advantage() = delta_at(0) includes infinity_mass so it is certified; docs/reference/accounting.md states exactly this contract.

Checked confidence-metadata algebra under composition (pld/mod.rs:475-483, 529-541): compose() adds failure probabilities (union bound, capped at 1) and combines resolutions as 1-(1-a)(1-b) matching Pmf infinity-mass composition; self_compose() keeps failure fixed -- verified this is statistically sound because on the confidence event the estimated single-step loss variable stochastically dominates the true one, dominance is preserved under independent convolution, and hockey-stick metrics are monotone under dominance (dominating-pair composition, Doroshenko et al. Connect-the-Dots framework); mc_resolution scales as 1-(1-r)^count; verified numerically via compiled module (self_compose(3): fail 0.01, res 0.01492; compose: fail 0.02, res 0.009974).

Checked the confidence parameter reaches the user-facing API: mc_resolution/mc_failure_probability/seed are constructor args of Rust and Python DiscretizationConfig (python/config.rs:29-53, core/discretization.py:32-39, set_discretization:97-148), per-query overrides on every DpProcess metric method (_base.py:146-367) and on pld_at of BMinSep/BallsInBins, and read back via Pld.mc_failure_probability/mc_confidence/mc_resolution/infinity_mass getters (python/pld.rs:79-105); epsilon_at auto-tightens resolution to min(mc_resolution, delta/2) (_base.py:209-216) so default settings cannot silently return inf at delta<=1e-5; docs (docs/reference/accounting.md, docs/user-guide/accounting.md, #748 additions) accurately describe the semantics including the 2,940,252-sample default count and the 'statistical confidence separate from DP delta' caveat.

Checked calibration selection effect (calibration.py:296-327): the configured failure probability is divided by probe_count = max_iterations + 2 for every adaptive probe via _use_discretization, the union bound over the two endpoint probes and up to max_iterations midpoints restores the overall level, the final PLD evaluation replays a probe deterministically (same config resolution min(probe_res, delta/2) as EpsilonBudget probes, same seed -> identical samples, no extra confidence event), and CalibrateResult.mc_failure_probability reports the overall budget covering the whole adaptive search; convergence is only accepted from the privacy-safe endpoint.

Checked Composed/Repeated failure budgeting (composition/_composed.py:64-88, _base.py repeated_pld:394-428): a composed process splits mc_failure_probability evenly and mc_resolution as 1-(1-r)^{1/groups} over top-level groups with recursive re-splitting for nested groups, while Repeated correctly does NOT split failure (one estimated PLD self-composed = one confidence event) and splits only resolution per release.

Checked balls-in-bins thread-count and seed reproducibility (the #331 fix): fixed 1024-sample shards with shard-index-only seeds and disjoint even/odd direction offsets (monte_carlo.rs:43-55), par_chunks_mut partition independent of the pool, par_sort making bucket construction order-invariant; verified by the in-tree Rust test test_bnb_mc_pld_is_identical_across_thread_counts and the subprocess test tests/test_balls_in_bins_reproducible.py (RAYON_NUM_THREADS 1/2/8).

Checked the identity-strategy BnB path bypasses Monte Carlo entirely (deterministic random-allocation transform, _balls_in_bins.py:205-214) with the exact G = E*I collapse re-derived; the K-prefix policy for correlated MC strategies (return the full-horizon confidence-bounded PLD for every nonzero prefix, _balls_in_bins.py:181-191 and _b_min_sep/__init__.py:144-155, registry.rs:78-83) is conservative by post-processing monotonicity and documented as deliberately loose (open issue #697 tracks tightening -- not re-reported).

Checked the transcript-reuse path consistency: registry K-prefix slicing (registry.rs:129-151) is a valid prefix projection because sample_x_under_p is causal, pld_from_transcripts' thread partition affects only sample order (sorted before banding), and the Python cache key includes resolved_num_mc_samples and seed so config changes force fresh corpora (thread-count gap reported as finding 2).
